[Item 1: Professor Wang's travel to Beijing for project seminar]
Step 1: Check — Is the 'Fudan University Business Trip Report Form' completed, signed by the head of the unit, and affixed with the official seal of the department/first-level budget unit?. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Are the inter-city transportation invoice and accommodation invoice both attached?. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Does the travel class comply with the standard for a traveler whose lodging standard is filled in at the bureau-director level? Bureau-director standard allows first-class train seating (first-class soft seat or first-class high-speed rail seat). Result: PASS.
Step 4: Compute — Accommodation standard: Beijing, bureau-director-level limit is 650 RMB/night (Appendix 1). Actual hotel rate is 600 RMB/night. Result: PASS.
Step 5: Compute — Meal allowance: 3 calendar days in Beijing (non-Xinjiang/Qinghai/Tibet) = 3 × 100 = 300 RMB. Claimed amount is 300 RMB. Result: PASS.
Step 6: Compute — City transportation: claimed 180 RMB with actual invoices. Cap is 80 RMB/day for 3 days = 240 RMB. 180 ≤ 240, and no self-driving/rental car. Result: PASS.
Step 7: Check — No external institution shared inter-city transportation, accommodation, meal, or city transportation expenses, so meal allowance and city transportation are allowable. Result: PASS.
Step 8: Check — Reservation reimbursement form and signatures on invoices are assumed to be included as part of standard reimbursement document preparation; no indication of missing signatures. Result: PASS.
Step 9: Conclusion — All travel reimbursement requirements are met with no deviations or missing items. Result: Fully Reimbursable.

[Item 2: Purchase of routine office supplies (stationery, newspapers, magazines)]
Step 1: Check — Are the purchased items routine office supplies not reaching the fixed asset threshold?. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Do the items fall within the Asset Management Office's review scope for purchased inventory? Case states they do not. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Has the seller provided a goods list together with the invoice, as required by Rule 6(2) for items not in the review scope?. Result: PASS.
Step 4: Check — No book, fixed asset, or printing-related requirements apply. Result: PASS.
Step 5: Check — Reservation reimbursement form and signatures are assumed to be included in standard reimbursement document preparation; no indication of missing signatures. Result: PASS.
Step 6: Conclusion — Office supplies reimbursement requirements are satisfied with all necessary materials provided. Result: Fully Reimbursable.

[Item 1: National Teaching Forum Conference Expenses]
Step 1: Check — Whether the expense qualifies as a conference under Rule 9. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Type of conference and applicable comprehensive quota standard. It is a domestic business conference (national teaching forum) funded by research project funds, so the standard is accommodation 500, meals 150, other expenses 100, total 750 RMB per person per day (Rule 9.1). Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Reported amounts: accommodation 500, meals 150, other expenses 110, total 760 per person per day. Compare with standard. Result: Other expenses exceed 100 by 10, total exceeds 750 by 10..
Step 4: Check — Rule 9.1 allows amounts to be adjusted among items within the comprehensive quota, but the total claimed (760) exceeds the maximum total (750). The excess cannot be covered by adjustment. Result: FAIL — total exceeds allowed comprehensive quota by 10 RMB per person per day..
Step 5: Check — Required materials (Rule 3): forum notice, agenda, budget form, detailed expense list, sign-in sheet, service invoices, original supporting documents, electronic settlement document, entrustment agreement all submitted. Result: PASS.
Step 6: Check — Conference duration (2 days, limit for domestic business conferences is 2 days per Rule 9.7), location (no prohibited scenic area, not majority Shanghai units outside Shanghai), no advance payment, no prohibited items. Result: PASS.
Step 7: Conclusion — The conference expense meets all procedural requirements but the claimed total exceeds the comprehensive quota by 10 RMB per person per day. Reimbursement must be capped at 750 per person per day; the excess is not reimbursable. Result: Partially Reimbursable.

[Item 2: Printing and Office Supplies for Conference Preparation]
Step 1: Check — Whether the expense falls under Rule 6 (office expenses/printing expenses) for printing of conference supplies and office stationery. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — According to Rule 6(5), for photocopying/printing fees where a single invoice or invoices in the same period total more than RMB 1,000, a detailed list is required. The case states the seller provided a goods list, but invoices were artificially split to avoid reaching the threshold that triggers the list requirement. Result: Artificially splitting invoices to circumvent the review threshold is explicitly prohibited..
Step 3: Check — Rule 6(5) further states: 'Invoice amounts shall not be artificially split in order to avoid the review requirement for providing a list.' The described action directly violates this prohibition. Result: FAIL.
Step 4: Check — Impact on reimbursement: artificial splitting undermines proper review and constitutes a procedural violation, making the entire expense item non-compliant regardless of whether a goods list was provided. Result: FAIL.
Step 5: Conclusion — Because invoice amounts were artificially split to avoid the review requirement, the expense does not comply with Rule 6(5). It is therefore not reimbursable. Result: Not Reimbursable.

[Item 1: University Financial Digitalization Training Program expenses]
Step 1: Check — Has the required 'Fudan University Detailed List of Training Expense Expenditures' been submitted?. Result: FAIL.
Step 2: Check — Does the total claimed (lodging 7,500 + meals 2,250 + venue/materials 1,200 + other 450 = 11,400, or the stated total 13,200) fall within the bureau‑director‑level comprehensive quota of 650 RMB/person/day × 15 days = 9,750?. Result: FAIL.
Step 3: Check — Is there any provision in Rule 10 allowing the comprehensive quota to be exceeded with a separate written approval?. Result: FAIL.
Step 4: Conclusion — The essential supporting document 'Fudan University Detailed List of Training Expense Expenditures' is missing, making the reimbursement package incomplete; even if provided, amounts exceed the standard quota without allowance for an increased standard. Therefore, this expense item cannot be reimbursed. Result: Not Reimbursable.

[Item 2: Beijing business trip travel expenses]
Step 1: Check — Has the 'Fudan University Business Trip Report Form' been signed by other relevant leaders since the traveler is the unit head?. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Does first‑class train seating comply with the transportation standard for bureau‑director‑level personnel (professor) under Rule 7(2)?. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Is the accommodation cost of 600 RMB/night within the Beijing bureau‑director‑level limit of 650 RMB/night (Appendix 1)?. Result: PASS.
Step 4: Check — Meal allowance claimed: 3 days × 100 RMB/day (other regions) = 300 RMB, matches the claimed 300 RMB. Result: PASS.
Step 5: Check — Lump‑sum city transportation allowance claimed: 3 days × 80 RMB/day = 240 RMB, matches the claimed 240 RMB, and no external unit bore the expense. Result: PASS.
Step 6: Conclusion — All reimbursement conditions are met: required approvals, transportation class, accommodation within limit, and correct allowances. No violations or missing materials. Result: Fully Reimbursable.

[Item 1: Family visit by married employee to visit spouse]
Step 1: Check — Whether the trip is a once-per-year family visit by a married employee to a spouse as allowed by Rule 11(1). Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Whether only intercity transportation is claimed and local transportation excluded, per Rule 11(3). Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Whether air travel was used but reimbursement is limited to the equivalent train fare, per Rule 11(3). The claimed amount is 950 RMB described as controlled to train fare. Result: PASS.
Step 4: Check — Whether the required 'Fudan University Faculty and Staff Family Visit Application and Approval Form' is present with departmental approval and HR seal, per Rule 11(4). Result: PASS.
Step 5: Check — Whether the printed 'Fudan University Reservation Reimbursement Form' bears signatures of the project principal investigator and handling staff member as required by Rule 3(1). The case does not mention this signature. Result: FAIL.
Step 6: Conclusion — Key material (signed reservation reimbursement form) is missing; therefore the expense item cannot be reimbursed. Result: Not Reimbursable.

[Item 2: Business trip to Beijing using research project funds]
Step 1: Check — Whether the 'Fudan University Business Trip Report Form' is completed, signed by unit head, and sealed by department, as per Rule 7(1). The traveler is not the unit head, so no countersignature issue. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Whether Professor Zhang qualifies for the transportation class used (first-class train seat). As a professor (bureau-director-level equivalent), first-class train/HSR is allowed per Rule 7(2). Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Accommodation standard: Beijing limit for bureau-director level is 650 RMB/night (Appendix 1). Claimed 700 RMB/night for 2 nights, exceeding by 50 RMB/night. Total excess = 100 RMB. Result: FAIL.
Step 4: Check — Meal allowance: 3 calendar days × 100 RMB/day (other regions) = 300 RMB. Claimed 300 RMB. No external unit bore meal costs. Result: PASS.
Step 5: Check — Local transportation: claimed 180 RMB against invoices. Invoices provided and amount within reasonable limits (3 days × 80 RMB lump-sum alternative = 240). No self-driving. Result: PASS.
Step 6: Check — Whether the printed reservation reimbursement form bears signatures of project PI and handling staff (Rule 3(1)). The case does not state that this signature requirement is met. Result: FAIL.
Step 7: Conclusion — Key material (signed reservation reimbursement form) is missing; therefore the entire expense item cannot be reimbursed, regardless of the accommodation excess. Result: Not Reimbursable.

[Item 1: Overseas Travel Expenses for Singapore Conference]
Step 1: Check — whether the Approval Document for Overseas Travel or Travel to Hong Kong and Macao from the Foreign Affairs Office is provided. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — whether the original overseas travel expense statement is included. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — whether the transportation class (economy airfare, hard‑seat train, third‑class ship) complies with the standard for other personnel under non‑research project funds (Rule 8(3)). Result: PASS.
Step 4: Check — whether air ticket and boarding pass are attached. Result: PASS.
Step 5: Check — whether the overseas expenses have been reviewed and signed by the Overseas Travel Service Center of the Foreign Affairs Office. Result: PASS.
Step 6: Check — whether original supporting invoices for lodging, conference registration fee, intercity transportation, visa fee, and insurance fee are present (Rule 3(2) and Rule 4(8)). Result: FAIL (explicitly stated as not seen).
Step 7: Check — whether the Fudan University Reservation Reimbursement Form bears signatures of the project principal investigator and handling staff member (Rule 3(1)). Result: FAIL (not mentioned, likely missing).
Step 8: Conclusion — The reimbursement is not compliant due to missing original invoices and the absence of required signatures on the Reimbursement Form, constituting incomplete procedures. Result: Not Reimbursable.

[Item 2: On‑Campus Academic Conference]
Step 1: Check — whether the per‑day amounts (accommodation 480, meals 150, other 100, total 730) fall within the research‑fund domestic business conference comprehensive quota (accommodation ≤500, meals ≤150, other ≤100, total ≤750). Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — whether all required supporting materials (notice, agenda, budget, detailed expenditure list, sign‑in sheet, service invoices, original documents, electronic settlement, entrustment agreement) are complete. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — whether the conference duration complies with Rule 9(7): domestic business conferences shall not exceed 2 days. Reported duration is 3 days. Result: FAIL.
Step 4: Check — whether reimbursement is in a single batch, with no advance payment and no foreign guests. These conditions are satisfied. Result: PASS.
Step 5: Conclusion — The total claim includes one day that exceeds the mandatory 2‑day limit. Only the expenses corresponding to the first two days are reimbursable; the third day’s expenses must be excluded. Result: Partially Reimbursable.

[Item 1: Doctoral Dissertation Defense Remuneration]
Step 1: Check — whether the reported amounts comply with Rule 13 (reviewers RMB 300–500, committee members RMB 300–500, secretary RMB 150). Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — whether the number of reviewers (5) and defense committee members (5) are within the allowed ranges (5–8 and 5–7). Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — whether the case description confirms that the reservation reimbursement form with the required signatures (project PI and handling staff) is present. Result: FAIL.
Step 4: Check — whether the remuneration declaration details (personnel category, bank transfer information, etc.) as required by Rule 12 are mentioned. Result: FAIL.
Step 5: Conclusion — The case omits essential reimbursement materials (reservation form, signatures) and declaration details, making the item non-reimbursable. Result: Not Reimbursable.

[Item 2: Special Lecture Fee for Invited Bureau-Director-Level Expert]
Step 1: Check — The lecturer is bureau-director level (equivalent to full senior professional title), so the lecture fee limit is RMB 1,000 per class hour. The declared fee is RMB 900 per class hour. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — The half-day lecture uses 4 class hours, which is the maximum allowed for a half day. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Rule 13 (2) requires lecture fees to be reported on an after-tax basis; the case explicitly states the fee was not reported as after-tax, so compliance with this requirement is unconfirmed. Result: FAIL.
Step 4: Check — The case does not mention the reservation reimbursement form, signatures, or any remuneration declaration details required by Rules 3 and 12. Result: FAIL.
Step 5: Conclusion — Due to missing essential materials and lack of clarity on after-tax reporting, the lecture fee cannot be reimbursed. Result: Not Reimbursable.

[Item 3: Conference Expenses (Non-Research Project Funds, Domestic Conference)]
Step 1: Check — All required materials (notice, agenda, budget, detailed list, sign-in sheet, invoices, etc.) are stated to be complete and expenses reimbursed in one batch. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Conference duration is 2 days. Rule 9 (7) allows 2 days for domestic business conferences but only 1 day for management conferences. Without knowing the nature, this is ambiguous, but for a non-research project conference it is likely a management conference, potentially violating the 1‑day limit. Result: FAIL.
Step 3: Check — Under non-research project funds, domestic conferences follow central government comprehensive quota standards. The highest category (Category I) allows accommodation 500, meals 150, other 110. The reported amounts: lodging 300 (OK), meals 200 (exceeds 150), other expenses 250 (exceeds 110). Result: FAIL.
Step 4: Check — Venue rental (200/person/day), equipment rental (100/person/day), and cold buffet reception (220/person/occasion) are separately listed, but they appear to overlap with items already covered under ‘other expenses’ or ‘meals’ in the comprehensive quota, constituting double charging and are not separately allowed for domestic conferences. Result: FAIL.
Step 5: Check — Staff board and lodging, volunteer subsidies, simultaneous interpretation, written translation, and vehicle expenses are itemized as if for an international conference (Appendix 2). For a domestic conference under non-research funds, these separate items are not provided for in the applicable rules and are therefore not reimbursable. Result: FAIL.
Step 6: Conclusion — The conference expense has multiple violations: the comprehensive quota for meals and other expenses is exceeded; separate venue, equipment, and reception charges are impermissible; and international‑conference‑specific items are not allowed. Only a portion of the accommodation cost and adjusted other expenses might be reimbursed after recalculation. Result: Partially Reimbursable.

[Item 1: Engineering Final Settlement Payment]
Step 1: Check — Whether the original approval form bears the official seal of the Capital Construction Office, the Project Review Seal of the Fudan University Renovation Management Office, and (since amount >100,000) the approval signatures of the director and the vice president in charge. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Because this is a final settlement, whether the originals of the Construction Project Cost Review Opinion (with cost review company seal and Capital Construction Office Review Process seal) and the Final Settlement Audit Filing Form (with signature/seal of the engineering management department and Audit Office receipt) are provided. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Whether the payment amount is based on the verified total settlement price, does not exceed the contract price, and there is no overpayment or advance payment ahead of progress. Result: PASS.
Step 4: Check — Whether the printed Fudan University Reservation Reimbursement Form with signatures of the project principal investigator and the handling staff member (Rule 3) has been submitted. Result: FAIL.
Step 5: Conclusion — The specific engineering final settlement requirements are met, but the case does not mention the mandatory general reimbursement form and signatures; this key material is missing. Result: Not Reimbursable.

[Item 2: Warranty Retention Refund]
Step 1: Check — Whether the warranty period has expired and there is no dispute over project quality. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Whether the warranty retention receipt issued by the Finance Office, signed by the department head, has been submitted. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Whether the printed Fudan University Reservation Reimbursement Form with required signatures (Rule 3) is included. Result: FAIL.
Step 4: Conclusion — The warranty retention refund conditions are satisfied, but the general reimbursement form and signatures are not mentioned; this missing key material prevents reimbursement. Result: Not Reimbursable.

[Item 3: Cost Review Fees (University Share)]
Step 1: Check — Whether the Construction Project Cost Review Opinion specifies the amount to be included in the university's construction cost. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Whether the claimed amount matches the university’s share, the contractor’s share is listed separately, and a copy of the cost review fee invoice in the contractor’s name is provided. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Whether the printed Fudan University Reservation Reimbursement Form with signatures of the project principal investigator and handling staff member (Rule 3) is present. Result: FAIL.
Step 4: Conclusion — The cost review fee requirements are fulfilled, but the general reimbursement form and required signatures are not mentioned; this key material is missing. Result: Not Reimbursable.

[Item 1: Purchase of laboratory equipment parts]
Step 1: Check — Whether the expense qualifies as purchased materials (not fixed assets or intangible assets) and the required 'Fudan University Purchased Inventory Confirmation Form (Based on Review Results)' is present. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Whether the case mentions a signed reservation reimbursement form and original invoices with required signatures as per Rule 3. Result: FAIL.
Step 3: Conclusion — Key general reimbursement materials (reservation form, signed invoices) are not evidenced; therefore this expense cannot be fully processed. Result: Not Reimbursable.

[Item 2: Travel expenses for laboratory equipment parts coordination trip]
Step 1: Check — Business Trip Report Form is completed, signed by unit head and affixed with official seal as per Rule 7(1). Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Professor Liu (a professor) used first-class train seat; under Rule 7(2) professors may be reimbursed for first-class soft seat/first-class high-speed rail seat. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Compute — Accommodation: 2 nights in Beijing at RMB 600/night vs. bureau-director-level standard of RMB 650/night (Appendix 1). Result: 600 ≤ 650, PASS.
Step 4: Compute — Meal allowance: 3 days × RMB 100/day (non-Xinjiang/Qinghai/Tibet) = RMB 300 claimed. Result: 300 = 300, PASS.
Step 5: Check — City transportation: actual receipts provided for RMB 180, allowed under Rule 7(9). Result: PASS.
Step 6: Check — Car rental/fuel/toll expenses totaling RMB 200: Rule 7(7) requires a special explanation approved and signed by project PI, which is missing. Result: FAIL.
Step 7: Check — Rule 7(10) would prohibit local transportation allowance if self-driving/rental, but actual city transportation is claimed, not an allowance, so no additional conflict. Result: PASS.
Step 8: Conclusion — All travel components are reimbursable except the car rental/fuel/toll costs, which lack required approval; the travel expense is therefore partially reimbursable. Result: Partially Reimbursable.

[Item 1: Visitor Reception Expenses]
Step 1: Check — whether the expense corresponds to domestic official hospitality under Rule 18, given the one-matter one-settlement handling, official letter, and the presence of the 'Fudan University Domestic Official Hospitality List'. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — whether all mandatory documents listed in Rule 18(1) are present: financial invoices, official letter, 'Fudan University Domestic Official Hospitality List', and 'Fudan University Domestic Official Hospitality Approval Form'. Result: FAIL.
Step 3: Conclusion — The 'Fudan University Domestic Official Hospitality Approval Form' is required but missing; thus the reimbursement package is incomplete and cannot be approved. Result: Not Reimbursable.

[Item 2: Special Conference Expenses]
Step 1: Check — expense type is a domestic business conference using research project funds, with accommodation and meals centrally arranged. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — reported daily per-person amounts against the research project conference quota: lodging 480 ≤ 500, meals 150 ≤ 150, other expenses 100 ≤ 100, total 730 ≤ 750. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — required materials per Rule 9(2): conference notice with agenda, budget form, detailed expense list, sign-in sheet with names and institutions, invoices, original supporting documents, electronic settlement slip, and entrustment agreement (contract); all are explicitly present. Result: PASS.
Step 4: Check — compliance with other procedural requirements: single-batch reimbursement, no advance payment, no foreign guests, duration 2 days (≤2 days for domestic business conference). Result: PASS.
Step 5: Conclusion — All relevant rule requirements are satisfied; the conference expenses are fully reimbursable. Result: Fully Reimbursable.

[Item 1: Large Centrifuge Maintenance Fee]

Step 2: Check — Is the original invoice for the maintenance service attached?. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Does the original invoice bear signatures of the project principal investigator and the handling staff member as required by Rule 3(2)?. Result: FAIL.
Step 4: Check — Is there evidence that a printed 'Fudan University Reservation Reimbursement Form' with the required signatures has been submitted as required by Rule 3(1)?. Result: FAIL.
Step 5: Conclusion — Key required materials are missing: invoice signatures and the reservation reimbursement form are not confirmed. Therefore, the expense is not reimbursable. Result: Not Reimbursable.

[Item 2: Office Supplies for Maintenance Ledger]
Step 1: Check — Does the amount reach the fixed asset threshold?. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Are the supplies within the Asset Management Office's review scope for purchased inventory?. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Has a goods list provided by the seller been attached with the invoice, satisfying Rule 6(2)?. Result: PASS.
Step 4: Check — Does the original invoice bear signatures of the project principal investigator and the handling staff member as required by Rule 3(2)?. Result: FAIL.
Step 5: Check — Is there evidence that a printed 'Fudan University Reservation Reimbursement Form' with the required signatures has been submitted as required by Rule 3(1)?. Result: FAIL.
Step 6: Conclusion — Despite meeting the specific office supplies requirements, the missing invoice signatures and unconfirmed reservation reimbursement form constitute missing key materials. The expense cannot be reimbursed in its current state. Result: Not Reimbursable.

[Item 1: Beijing Business Trip]
Step 1: Check — whether the 'Fudan University Business Trip Report Form' is attached. Result: FAIL.
Step 2: Check — whether the intercity transportation invoice and lodging invoice are present. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Conclusion — the mandatory Business Trip Report Form is missing, making the entire travel expense reimbursement unprocessable. Result: Not Reimbursable.

[Item 2: Visitor Reception - Lodging]

Step 2: Check — the hotel class is four-star, which meets the Appendix 3 standard for ordinary foreign guest delegations. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — no evidence of over-standard amount or missing invoices. Result: PASS.
Step 4: Conclusion — all requirements are satisfied; lodging expense is fully reimbursable. Result: Fully Reimbursable.

Step 1: Check — the Overseas Expert Work Expense Accounting Report is present and properly signed. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — the transportation arrangement is consistent with the guests' rank (other personnel), and no evidence of class exceedance. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Conclusion — intercity transportation expense complies with standards and is fully reimbursable. Result: Fully Reimbursable.

[Item 4: Visitor Reception - Routine Meal Expenses]
Step 1: Check — required report and signatures are complete. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — the applicable standard for other personnel is RMB 300 per person per day. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — the reported amount is RMB 320 per person per day, exceeding the standard by RMB 20. Result: FAIL.
Step 4: Conclusion — only RMB 300 per person per day can be reimbursed; the excess is not reimbursable. Result: Partially Reimbursable.

[Item 5: Visitor Reception - Banquet Expenses]
Step 1: Check — accounting report and signatures are complete. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — the reported banquet cost is RMB 280 per person per occasion, which is within the RMB 300 limit. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Conclusion — banquet expense meets the standard and is fully reimbursable. Result: Fully Reimbursable.

[Item 6: Visitor Reception - City Transportation]
Step 1: Check — required report is in order. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — the city transportation arrangement matches the guests' rank and no over‑standard usage is indicated. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Conclusion — city transportation expense is compliant and fully reimbursable. Result: Fully Reimbursable.

[Item 7: Visitor Reception - Gift Expenses]
Step 1: Check — accounting report is complete and signed. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — the gifts are controlled at RMB 180 per person per occasion, which is modest and below the bureau‑director‑level cap of RMB 200. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — the recipients are 'other personnel', and small commemorative gifts are permitted. Result: PASS.
Step 4: Conclusion — gift expenses are within an appropriate range and are fully reimbursable. Result: Fully Reimbursable.

[Item 8: Visitor Reception - Staff Meal Allowance Subsidy]
Step 1: Check — required report and signatures are present. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — the reported subsidy is exactly RMB 50 per person per occasion, matching the Appendix 3 limit. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Conclusion — staff meal allowance subsidy complies with the rule and is fully reimbursable. Result: Fully Reimbursable.

[Item 1: Warranty retention refund]
Step 1: Check — Whether the warranty period has expired and no quality dispute arose during the warranty period. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Whether the warranty retention receipt, duly signed by the department head, is attached. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Whether the absence of the 'Fudan University Construction Project Cost Review Opinion' and a copy of the cost review fee invoice violates any requirement for the warranty retention refund under Rule 15. Result: Not Applicable — These documents are required for cost review fee reimbursement (Rule 15(2)), not for the warranty retention refund (Rule 15(1))..
Step 4: Conclusion — All materials specifically required for the warranty retention refund are present and meet Rule 15(1); the refund is fully reimbursable. Result: Fully Reimbursable.

[Item 2: Initial project payment for library floor repair]
Step 1: Check — Whether the project exceeds RMB 100,000 and the approval form bears the signatures of the Capital Construction Office director and the vice president in charge. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Whether the original approval form bears the official seal of the Capital Construction Office and the Project Review Seal of the Fudan University Renovation Management Office. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Whether this application is for the initial payment and the original construction contract is attached. Result: PASS.
Step 4: Check — Whether the payment amount conforms to the contract and project progress, with no overpayment or advance payment. Result: PASS.
Step 5: Check — Whether any mandatory large‑payment form is missing (the provided approval form for engineering projects already fulfills the large‑payment form requirement under Rule 3(5)). Result: PASS.
Step 6: Conclusion — All requirements of Rule 14 and relevant supplementary rules are met; the initial payment is fully reimbursable. Result: Fully Reimbursable.

[Item 1: Family Visit Travel Expense]
Step 1: Check — Eligibility: married employee visiting spouse, one round‑trip per year. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Transportation mode and amount: actual air travel, but claimed amount limited to equivalent train fare (RMB 950). Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Expense composition: only inter‑city transportation, no local transportation expenses. Result: PASS.
Step 4: Check — The ‘Fudan University Faculty and Staff Family Visit Application and Approval Form’ has departmental approval and the personnel department seal. Result: PASS.
Step 5: Check — General reimbursement materials (reservation form, required signatures) – no indication of missing documents. Result: PASS.
Step 6: Conclusion — All applicable requirements are met; the full claimed amount (RMB 950) is reimbursable. Result: Fully Reimbursable.

[Item 2: Long‑term Training Expenses]
Step 1: Check — Training information: Professor Zhao attended a 40‑day training; classification as bureau‑director‑level standard. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Number of trainees: the expenses are reported for the trainee himself (one person). Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Training days exceed 30: 40 days → 10 excess days; the 70% quota rule (Rule 10(2)) applies. Result: PASS.
Step 4: Compute — Maximum reimbursable lodging: first 30 days: 30×400 = 12 000; excess 10 days at 70%: 10×280 = 2 800; total = 14 800. Result: 14 800.
Step 5: Compute — Maximum reimbursable meals: 30×150 = 4 500 + 10×105 = 1 050 → 5 550. Result: 5 550.
Step 6: Compute — Maximum reimbursable venue/materials/transport: 30×70 = 2 100 + 10×49 = 490 → 2 590. Result: 2 590.
Step 7: Compute — Maximum reimbursable other expenses: 30×30 = 900 + 10×21 = 210 → 1 110. Result: 1 110.
Step 8: Check — Claimed amounts: lodging 18 000 > 14 800; meals 6 750 > 5 550; venue etc. 3 150 > 2 590; other 1 350 > 1 110; total 29 250 > 24 050 (sum of maxima). Therefore, amounts exceed the regulatory quotas. Result: FAIL.
Step 9: Check — Required supporting materials: ‘Fudan University Detailed List of Training Expense Expenditures’, trainee list and contact info, and service provider’s detailed expense statement are provided. Result: PASS.
Step 10: Conclusion — The expenses are only partially reimbursable; reimbursement must be limited to the standard caps (total 24 050 RMB), and the excess amounts cannot be reimbursed. Result: Partially Reimbursable.

[Item 1: Overseas travel expenses for international academic conference]
Step 1: Check — The approval document is from the Exit and Entry Center of the Foreign Affairs Office, but Rule 8(1) requires the document to be issued by the Overseas Affairs Center of the Foreign Affairs Office. Result: FAIL.
Step 2: Check — The overseas travel expense statement is included as required by Rule 8(1). Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Air ticket and boarding pass are provided as required by Rule 8(2). Result: PASS.
Step 4: Check — Formal invoices for lodging, conference registration fee, intercity transportation, visa fee, and insurance fee are not seen, contravening Rule 3(2) which requires original invoices. Result: FAIL.
Step 5: Check — The expenses were reviewed and signed by the Exit and Entry Service Center, but Rule 8(2) requires review and signature by the Overseas Travel Service Center; moreover, review and signature do not replace the missing invoices. Result: FAIL.
